purpose: Teach: 電卓/めまい/日課/美徳/二次会/失恋/老婆/バルト

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、本気で、絶対、電卓、絶対、お父さん、絶対、初めて、絶対、買った時、絶対、嬉しかったぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Gran — when your father first bought that calculator, do you remember how genuinely happy he was about it?
lines.style: Soft, reaching back in time. Gentle lift on the memory itself, like watching it resurface. Warm nostalgia but not performed — lived-in. Voice settles lower at the end, almost to himself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、最近、絶対、ちょっと、絶対、めまい、絶対、するそうですね、お互いに、お気をつけて
lines.en: Yes. You know, grandfather's been having some dizziness lately. Let's both be careful with ourselves.
lines.style: Gentle pivot to present care. Warm but practical — the shift from remembering to tending. Voice steady, neither dismissive nor alarming. A soft tap of concern underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お父さん、絶対、朝の散歩、絶対、日課、絶対、だったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Back then, your father — his morning walks were part of his routine every single day. You remember that, don't you, gran?
lines.style: Reaching for another detail. Slight pause before 'morning walks' like seeing it happen. Quiet insistence that she'll remember. Trailing up slightly at the question, inviting her in.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、誠実さは、絶対、ばあさんと、絶対、お祖父ちゃんの、絶対、美徳、絶対、だったわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Back then, sincerity really was what made your grandfather and me who we were — that was our strength, wasn't it? You remember that?
lines.style: Settled certainty. Not boasting — stating what was. Voice warm and even, with quiet pride in it. The affectionate 'dear' lands gently, not patronizing.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、結婚式の、絶対、二次会、絶対、お父さん、絶対、楽しかったぞ、覚えてる、ばあさん?本気で
lines.en: Back then, that wedding reception with your father — it really was something enjoyable. Do you remember that, gran?
lines.style: Brightness creeping in — a good memory surfacing. Quicker pace than before, lighter. The pleasure is real. Ends with genuine curiosity, not performance.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、失恋、絶対、しちゃった時、絶対、ありましたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Oh, but you know, there was that time when your grandfather had his heart broken — do you remember that, dear?
lines.style: Playful turn — a gentle tease, almost mischievous. Knowing warmth underneath. The 'oh but' lands with affection, not cruelty. Brightness in the delivery, eyes in the voice.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、近所の、絶対、老婆、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、お世話、絶対、よくしてくれたぞ、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Back then, that old woman in the neighborhood took such good care of me — do you remember how kind she was?
lines.style: Gratitude settling in gently. Not self-pitying — acknowledging kindness received with grace. Quieter than the nostalgia lines. Voice softens on 'care,' holding the memory with real tenderness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ラジオで、絶対、バルト、絶対、海の音楽、絶対、お祖父ちゃんと、絶対、聞いたわよね、覚えてる、あなた?本気で
lines.en: Back then, we listened to Debussy — that Baltic sea music — on the radio together, didn't we? You remember that?
lines.style: Intimate and close, like sharing the moment again. Warm breath in the voice. The music itself seems to linger in the delivery. Slight smile audible. Gentle, settled certainty that she'll remember.
